stem:
A 20-year-old student examines a histology slide of a muscle that is striated, contracts without voluntary input, and has cells joined end-to-end by specialized junctions.

Which of the following muscle types is she viewing?

options.label: A
options.misconception: The other striated type is being chosen despite the involuntary control.
options.explanation: Skeletal muscle is striated and multinucleated, but it requires signaling from the nervous system to trigger contraction (voluntary) and lacks intercalated discs.

options.label: B
options.misconception: The involuntary visceral type is being chosen despite the striations.
options.explanation: Smooth muscle is involuntary but nonstriated and mononucleated; the striations on the slide exclude it.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; striated plus involuntary plus intercalated junctions is cardiac muscle.
options.explanation: Cardiac muscle is striated, under involuntary control, and its cells are joined at intercalated discs containing gap junctions and desmosomes, contracting as one unit under pacemaker regulation.

options.label: D
options.misconception: A smooth-muscle subtype is being chosen despite the striations.
options.explanation: Visceral (single-unit) smooth muscle contracts as a unit through gap junctions, but it is nonstriated; the slide shows a striated tissue.

options.label: E
options.misconception: A rare smooth-muscle subtype is being chosen despite the striations.
options.explanation: Multiunit smooth muscle (e.g. in the skin at hair follicles) is nonstriated; it cannot account for the striated appearance.

context: Learning objective: tell the three muscle types apart. Skeletal: striated, multinucleated, voluntary (needs motor-neuron signaling). Cardiac: striated, involuntary, intercalated discs, pacemaker-driven, contracts as one unit. Smooth: nonstriated, mononucleated, involuntary; single-unit (visceral) fibers joined by gap junctions.
